title: Warning signs
objectives: Name five warning signs in a withdrawal plan.
Say what to discuss when the rate is above 6–7%.
body_md:
Warning signs: a withdrawal rate above 6–7%, no health insurance, no emergency fund, large dependants' needs, or all money in a single asset class. When the rate is above 6–7%, discuss lower spending, other income, or delaying extras — and show, illustratively, how quickly the money may run out. Do not promise it will last.

> **Investor takeaway:** A withdrawal rate above 6–7% is a warning sign, not a plan.
example: Mrs. Rao wants ₹80,000 a month from ₹1 Cr: ≈ 9.6% rate — show how quickly it may run out (illustrative) and discuss lower spending or other income.
say: A withdrawal rate above 6–7% is a warning sign.
No health insurance and no emergency fund are warning signs.
never: A 9.6% rate is fine if the client is optimistic.
